The flowchart, titled "MINOR LOCP ERROR MONITOR (EC)", begins with a "START EC400" block. It leads to a decision diamond: "RESOLVER COUNT EXCEED LIMIT 1". If the answer is "NO", the process proceeds to "RESET RSBLNS COUNTER" and then "EXIT RETURN". If the answer is "YES", it moves to a second decision diamond: "RESOLVER COUNT EXCEED LIMIT 2". From this second diamond, a "YES" path leads to "SET CHANNEL A & B FAILURE BITS IN MC24", and a "NO" path leads to "SET CHANNEL B FAILURE BIT IN MODE CODE 24". The "SET CHANNEL A & B FAILURE BITS IN MC24" block has a feedback loop back to the "SET CHANNEL B FAILURE BIT IN MODE CODE 24" block. From "SET CHANNEL B FAILURE BIT IN MODE CODE 24", the process continues to "SET RSBLNS COUNTER FOR CHANNEL TO ZERO" and finally "EXIT RETURN".

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: This module will schedule the time of execution of various time base referenced functions specified in a mission dependent table. When the time for execution of a scheduled event occurs, the Events Processor will give control to the appropriate event submodule which will perform the actual function.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: M.EP00 Entered from Timer 2 when the time for a scheduled function occurs.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: M.EP05 Entered from the Time Base Set module for proper initialization of the events table at each time base change.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The table advance pointers L.ER00 and L.TBR0 must be initialized to the first event table entry. Variable HOP constants for the entries in the Timed Events Table which are affected by the mode of operation (Flight or Flight Simulation) must be initialized according to the mode of operation selected. For example, the entries for the timed start of time bases are active only for the Repeatable Flight Simulation Mode. *

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: There is an event submodule, L.Exxx, for each entry in the Timed Events Tables. These modules perform time referenced mission dependent functions such as enabling and inhibiting discretes, queuing of modules, setting reasonableness test constants, etc.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The Timed Events Table is sub-divided according to time bases. Events which are referenced to a specific time base will only be processed in that time base. Any events which are scheduled but not processed are bypassed at the time base end.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Each Timed Events Table entry is composed of two words. The first word is a HPC to the event subroutine. The second word contains the time of execution referenced from time base start (RTCP scaled B27).

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: A detailed description of the mission dependent events required for this mission are given in the Events Processor Timed Events Table and the flowcharts of the Events Processor Submodules in Part IV.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Fixed Point Divide Utility is to perform a divide operation with specified inputs and to delay the proper time for the DIV instruction to operate.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Upon entry, the numerator is to be in accumulator. Upon exit, the quotient will be in PQ and accumulator.

chunks.label: Diagram
chunks.content:
graph TD; A[START U.FD00] --> B[SAVE RETURN LINKAGE]; B --> C[PERFORM DIVIDE]; C --> D[DELAY FOR DIVIDE EXECUTION TIME]; D --> E[PLACE DIVIDE RESULT IN ACCUMULATOR]; E --> F[EXIT RETURN];

The flowchart consists of six rectangular boxes with dotted borders, arranged vertically. Each box contains text describing a step in the process. The steps are connected by vertical dotted lines, with a small 'V' character centered on each line. The steps are: 1. START U.FD00, 2. SAVE RETURN LINKAGE, 3. PERFORM DIVIDE, 4. DELAY FOR DIVIDE EXECUTION TIME, 5. PLACE DIVIDE RESULT IN ACCUMULATOR, and 6. EXIT RETURN. The label 'U.FD00' is positioned to the left of the first step.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of this utility module is to perform either an absolute freeze or a command freeze of the vehicle.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
U.FR00Entered by the Orbit Guidance module to perform an absolute freeze*
U.FR10Entered from Non-Interrupt Sequencer modules to perform a command freeze

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
D.FLTFlight Mode indicator
D.VTHXTotal roll gimbal angle*
D.VTHYTotal Pitch gimbal angle*
D.VTHZTotal Yaw gimbal angle*
D.VCCXCommanded Chi X (Rate limited roll gimbal angle)*
D.VCCYCommanded Chi Y (Rate limited pitch gimbal angle)*
D.VCCZCommanded Chi Z (Rate limited yaw gimbal angle)*

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
D.VCCXCommanded Chi X (Rate limited roll gimbal angle)*
D.VCCYCommanded Chi Y (Rate limited pitch gimbal angle)*
D.VCCZCommanded Chi Z (Rate limited yaw gimbal angle)*

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
D.VGCX Guidance Chi X (Desired roll gimbal angle) *
D.VGCY Guidance Chi Y (Desired pitch gimbal angle) *
D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle) *
D.VDCX Delta Chi X (Roll commanded chi increment) *
D.VDCY Delta Chi Y (Pitch commanded chi increment) *
D.VDCZ Delta Chi Z (Yaw commanded chi increment) *
D.FDCO Bypass setting delta chi flag

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: For an absolute freeze in the Flight Mode, the command chi's and guidance chi's are set to the current gimbal angles. The delta chi's are set to zero. When in the Flight Simulation Mode, these quantities are not set.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: For a command freeze in the Flight Mode, the guidance chi's are set to the command chi's and the delta chi's are set to zero. When in the Flight Simulation Mode, these quantities are not set.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: When setting the guidance chi's, command chi's, and delta chi's, the program must be under interrupt protection.

chunks.label: Diagram
chunks.content:
graph TD
    subgraph U_FROO [U.FROO]
        S1[START U.FROO] --> E1[ENTRY FOR ABSOLUTE FREEZE]
        E1 --> D1{FLIGHT SIMULATION MODE}
        D1 -- YES --> E1R1[EXIT RETURN]
        D1 -- NO --> FR20
    end
    subgraph U_FR10 [U.FR10]
        S2[START U.FR10] --> E2[ENTRY FOR COMMAND FREEZE]
        E2 --> D2{FLIGHT SIMULATION MODE}
        D2 -- YES --> E1R2[EXIT RETURN]
        D2 -- NO --> FR20

The left path starts with a "START IN022" block, followed by a computation block "(U, SC00) COMPUTE SIN/CCS OF DESCENDING NODE", then a telemetry block "(U, TRC0) TELEMETER DESCENDING NODE", then another computation block "(U, SC01) COMPUTE SIN/COS OF INCLINATION ANGLE", then a block "SET ELEMENT A11 = CCS (DESCENDING NODE)", then "SET ELEMENT A12 = 0", then "SET ELEMENT A33 = COS(INCLIN ANG) * CCS(DES NODE)", then "SET ELEMENT A13 = SIN (INCLINATION ANGLE)", then "SET ELEMENT A22 = COS (INCLINATION ANGLE)", and finally "SET ELEMENT A33 = -COS(INCLIN ANG) * SIN(DES NCDE)". The right path starts with a "START IN022" block, followed by "SET ELEMENT A32 = SIN (INCLINATION ANGLE)", then "SET ELEMENT A23 = -SIN(INCLIN ANG) * CCS(DES NODE)", then "SET ELEMENT A21 = SIN(INCLIN ANG) * SIN(DES NODE)", then a telemetry block "(U, TRC1) TELEMETER INCLINATION ANGLE", and finally "EXIT IN23". There are two feedback loops: one from the final block of the left path back to the "START IN022" block of the right path, labeled "BO:"; and another from the "START IN022" block of the left path to the "SET ELEMENT A32 = SIN (INCLINATION ANGLE)" block of the right path, also labeled "BO:".

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Natural Logarithm Utility is to compute the natural logarithm of the quotient of two specified numbers by means of an algorithm which utilizes a polynomial approximation to the natural logarithm function.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Upon entry, two input arguments of identical scaling must be specified. The accumulator must contain the numerator value (ARG1), and the PQ must contain the denominator value (ARG2)

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Liftoff Search module is to monitor the discrete input register for indication of vehicle liftoff (DI 24 or DI 7) and on detecting either discrete, access the Time Base 1 module to initiate Time Base 1.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: M.L000 Entered from Timer 1 every 40 milliseconds from GRR + 17.4 seconds until Time Base 1 is initiated.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
M.ML20 Minor Loop
M.TB15 Time Base 1
U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
D.VTRS RTC reading to be used by the Control Program Time Update routine at a new time base start.
D.VTBI Indication of time base initiation *

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The Liftoff Search module is activated by the Events Processor at 17.4 seconds after GRR by altering the Timer 1 HPC value, D.GML, to M.L000 for the Liftoff Search module instead of the Minor Loop module. Liftoff Search accesses Minor Loop on each entry so that Minor Loop continues to execute at a 40 millisecond rate. The Time Base 1 module deactivates Liftoff Search by resetting the Timer 1 HPC to M.ML00 for Minor Loop.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: On entry, the Liftoff Search module checks for liftoff. If liftoff has not occurred, it accesses Minor Loop and then repeats the check for liftoff. Since the Minor Loop operation requires approximately 20 milliseconds, the effective rate of checking for liftoff is every 20 milliseconds.

The flowchart, titled "LIFT-OFF SEARCH (LO)", describes a process for monitoring and responding to lift-off events. It begins at M.L000 with a "START" block. The first step is to "READ DISCRETE INPUT REGISTER" (L010). This leads to a decision point: "LIFT OFF DISCRETE 'A' SET". If "YES", it proceeds to L045. If "NO", it moves to "LIFT OFF DISCRETE 'B' SET". If "YES" here, it goes to L040. If "NO", it enters a loop: "[M.M120] EXECUTE MINOR LOOP", followed by another "READ DISCRETE INPUT REGISTER" and a decision "LIFT OFF DISCRETE 'C' SET". If "YES" here, it goes to L045. chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: This module is executed only in the Flight Simulation Mode of program operation. It requires as input the Ladder Ramp Table (see attached format).

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Both the ladder rate and magnitude are limited by the Minor Loop module according to the maximum limits specified for control of the ladder outputs in a mission dependent table.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The Ladder Ramp Table is sub-divided according to time bases. If a requested ramp cannot be completed within the current time base, the processing of the ramp is cancelled and the ladders are zeroed. The ramps referenced to the new time base are then started.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: If two ramps are requested too close together, the second ramp will be superimposed on the first. *

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The Ladder Ramp Table is composed of two words per entry. The format for each entry is as follows:

chunks.label: Table
chunks.content:
Word 1 Ladder ramp
Word 2 Ramp occurrence time

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: B = Specifies pitch, roll, yaw or combined ladder ramp.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: C = Specifies the ladder rate in degrees per second.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D = Specifies the ladder magnitude in degrees.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Where F = The time for the ramp to occur in real time clock pulses scaled B27, referenced from time base.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The Minor Loop module has four functions:

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
1. (1) To read platform gimbal angles, to compute yaw, roll and pitch attitude corrections needed to drive the gimbals to the desired position, and to output these commands to the LVDA.
  2. (2) To perform various tests on the platform gimbal to verify the hardware in the LVDA and the ST-124M platform.
  3. (3) To insure that the gimbal reads and attitude error commands will be telemetered by the DOM.
  4. (4) To access the Cutoff Logic module when requested.

The flowchart, titled "MINOR LOOP (ML)", describes a control sequence for a minor loop. It begins with two parallel start points: "START M.ML000" and "START M.ML20". The "START M.ML000" path leads to "FLT SIM MINOR LOOP ENTRY", which then branches into a decision: "IS A LADDER RAMP BEING COMMANDED". If "NO", it proceeds to "ML00 UPDATE COMM. CH1'S BY DELTA CH1'S EQ.8-2-1". If "YES", it goes to "ML00 DECREMENT COUNTER FOR CH1 UPDATES" and then loops back to "START M.ML000". The "START M.ML20" path leads to "NORMAL ENTRY FOR MINOR LOOP PROCESSING", which also leads to "ML00 UPDATE COMM. CH1'S BY DELTA CH1'S EQ.8-2-1". From this point, it reaches a decision: "GIMBAL RTC TO BE ALTERED". If "NO", it exits via "ML299 EXIT RETURN". If "YES", it proceeds to "ML500 ALTER GIMBAL RTC'S CHECK" and loops back to "ML00 UPDATE COMM. CH1'S BY DELTA CH1'S EQ.8-2-1". The "START M.ML20" path also leads to "ML100 PROCESS PITCH (Y) AXIS", which leads to "ML200 PROCESS ROLL (X) AXIS", then "ML260 VERIFY DOM ISSUED PROPERLY", and finally "ML299 EXIT RETURN". The "ML091 HAS CONVERTER B BEEN SELECTED" decision point branches based on whether a converter has been selected. If "NO", it goes to "ML090 RESCHEDULE MINOR LOOP" and loops back to "START M.ML000". If "YES", it goes to "ML100 SET ICR TO SELECT CONVERTER A" and loops back to "ML091 HAS CONVERTER B BEEN SELECTED".

    Start1[START ML620] --> ErrorTE[ERROR TELEMETRY ENTRY (PITCH)]
    Start2[START ML621] --> BackupGimbal[BACKUP GIMBAL TEST ENTRY (PITCH)]
    Start3[ALTER Y GIMBAL PIO TO BACKUP REQUEST] --> AlterCoarse[ALTER COARSE GIMBAL, 180 DEG OVERFLOWS]
    
    ErrorTE --> UseTag1[USE TAG FOR Y GIMBAL RSBINS TEST FAILURE]
    BackupGimbal --> UseTag2[USE TAG FOR Y GIMBAL ZPRO TEST FAILURE]

The flowchart, titled "MINOR LOOP (ML)", describes a process for handling multiplexer failures. It begins with "START ML650", followed by "MULTIPLEXER FAILURE TEST". The next step is "RESET A MULTIPLEXER FAILURE RATE". This is followed by "SET MULTIPLEXER FAILURE FLAG TO NI". A decision point then asks "HAS A MULTIPLEXER FAILED?". If the answer is "YES", the process proceeds to "SET ICR TO SWITCH GIMBAL ORDER", then "MAINTAIN ICR STATUS WORD", and "SET A MULTIPLEXER FAILURE IN MC24". This is followed by "LOCK OFF DG PROCESSOR". If the answer to the decision point is "NO", the process proceeds directly to "EXIT RETURN". A return path from "LOCK OFF DG PROCESSOR" also leads to "EXIT RETURN". The label "ML655" is located near the bottom left of the flowchart.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Matrix Multiply Utility module is to compute the product of two specified matrices.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Two arguments must be supplied upon entry:

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
1. (1) The accumulator must contain a computer word of the form CLA A; MPY B, where A and B are the initial locations of the matrices to be multiplied.
  2. (2) The PQ must contain a computer word of the form STO C in syllable 1 and a counter (scaled B25) in syllable 0. C must be the initial location of the matrix in which the product matrix is to be stored.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Upon exit, the resultant product matrix will be stored in the matrix specified by the computer word in the PQ.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: All matrices must be grouped in vector form. Each column or row is to be stored as a vector using the VEC assembler pseudo operation. The three vectors required to represent a 3x3 matrix must be stored using the MAT assembler pseudo operation.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The A matrix must be stored by rows and the B matrix by columns. The resultant C matrix will be stored by columns.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Since utility modules may not normally access each other, this module saves its return linkage and sets up the necessary linkage to use the Vector Dot Product Utility.

The flowchart illustrates the 'MATRIX MULTIPLY UTILITY (MM)'. It begins with a 'START' block labeled 'U,MM00'. The first step is to 'SAVE RETURN LINKAGES AND INPUT ARGUMENTS'. This is followed by a loop starting with 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT'. Inside the loop, the first element is stored, followed by another 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT', then the second element is stored, followed by a third 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT', and finally the third element is stored. A decision point 'MATRIX MULTIPLICATION COMPLETE' follows. If the answer is 'NO', the process moves to 'MM200 SET TO FORM ELEMENTS FOR NEXT ROW' and then loops back to the first 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT' step. If the answer is 'YES', the process proceeds to 'EXIT RETURN'. The 'R2' register is indicated as being used in the 'MM100' steps.

The flowchart, titled "MINOR LOOP SUPPORT (MS)", outlines a sequence of processing steps. It begins at MS100, which involves commanding the yaw gimbal. This is followed by MS200, where delta chi values are computed. The process then moves to MS210 to read the roll gimbal angle from the telemetry. At MS250, a decision is made regarding the limit of delta chi. If the limit is exceeded (N3), the flow proceeds to MS300; otherwise (YES), it also proceeds to MS300. MS300 involves inhibiting delta chi and computing SMC compensation. The flow then continues to MS320 to read the pitch gimbal angle, followed by MS400 to compute sine and cosine coefficients, MS430 to handle minor loop support items, and finally MS450 to exit and return.

The flowchart, titled "MINOR LOOP SUPPORT (MS)", begins at a "START MSS70" block. It proceeds to a decision diamond: "IS DELTA CHI VALUE NEGATIVE". If "YES", it goes to an "EXIT RETURN" block. If "NO", it moves to another decision diamond: "IS DELTA CHI VALUE GREATER THAN THE LIMIT". If "YES" here, it goes to a process block "MS510 SET DELTA CHI = + LIMIT", then to a process block "SET SMC FLAG FOR LIMITED CHI", and finally to an "EXIT RETURN" block. If "NO" here, it goes directly to an "EXIT RETURN" block. From the "NO" path of the second decision, it moves to a third decision diamond: "IS DELTA CHI GREATER THAN THE LIMIT". If "YES" here, it goes to a process block "MS520 SET DELTA CHI = - LIMIT", then to a process block "SET SMC FLAG FOR LIMITED CHI", and finally to an "EXIT RETURN" block. If "NO" here, it goes directly to an "EXIT RETURN" block. The "NO" path from the third decision also leads to the "EXIT RETURN" block.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Matrix Transpose Utility module is to form and store the transpose of a specified matrix.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: U.MT00 Entered by any Non-Interrupt Sequencer and Periodic Processor module.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Upon entry, a computer word of the form STO B; CLA A must be in the accumulator, where A is the initial location of the matrix to be transposed and B is the initial location of the matrix in which the transpose is to be stored.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Both matrices are to be grouped in vector form using the VEC assembler pseudo-operation. The three vectors required to represent a 3x3 matrix must be stored using the MAT assembler pseudo-operation.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The matrices A and B may be the same. In that case, the A matrix is transposed and the transpose is then stored over A. Matrices may be grouped by either column or row vectors.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Upon exit, the transposed matrix will be stored in the matrix specified by the word on entry.

chunks.content:
graph TD; A[START U.MT00] --> B[SAVE RETURN LINKAGE AND INPUT ARGUMENTS]; B --> C[FORM TRANSPOSE MATRIX]; C --> D[EXIT RETURN];

The flowchart consists of four rectangular boxes with dotted borders, arranged vertically. The first box contains the text "START U.MT00". A vertical dotted line with a downward-pointing arrow connects it to the second box, which contains "SAVE RETURN LINKAGE AND INPUT ARGUMENTS". Another vertical dotted line with a downward-pointing arrow connects the second box to the third box, which contains "FORM TRANSPOSE MATRIX". A final vertical dotted line with a downward-pointing arrow connects the third box to the fourth box, which contains "EXIT RETURN".

The flowchart, titled "ORBIT NAVIGATION (NZ)", details the process of updating and correcting orbit navigation data. It begins with "START NZ011" and proceeds to a "NAVIGATION UPDATE PASS". If successful, it moves to a "PREDICTOR NAVIGATION PASS". If not, it calculates midpoint velocity and positions (NZ021), resets the navigation update pass indication (NZ090), and sets a flag for the predicted endpoint pass (NZ100). This leads to computing gravitational acceleration (NZ120) and drag acceleration (NZ130), which then feeds into the "CAL ACCEL DUE TO GRAVITY AND DRAG" step (NZ131) before returning to the predictor pass. If the predictor pass fails, it calculates corrected endpoint velocity and position (NZ201), sets a flag for the corrected endpoint pass (NZ250), and calculates predicted endpoint velocity and position (NZ301). This leads to setting a flag for the corrected endpoint pass (NZ350) and finally the endpoint pass (NZ401), which also feeds into the gravitational acceleration calculation (NZ120). The process concludes with "EXIT NZ500".

The flowchart, titled "ORBIT ACCELERATIONS (OA)", consists of four main steps connected by vertical arrows. The first step is a start box labeled "START M_OA00". A vertical arrow labeled "V" leads to the second step, a box labeled "OA00: SET UP FOR COMP. DRAG COMPONENTS". Another vertical arrow labeled "V" leads to the third step, a box labeled "OA014: COMPUTE DRAG ACCELERATION COMPONENTS". A final vertical arrow labeled "V" leads to the fourth step, an exit box labeled "OA25: EXIT RETURN".

chunks.content:
graph TD
    START_OA01[START OA01] --> MID_PASS{MID-POINT PASS}
    MID_PASS -- YES --> CORR_PASS{CORRECTOR END-POINT NAVIGATION PASS}
    MID_PASS -- NO --> OBTAIN_END[OBTAIN END-POINT GIMBAL ANGLES]
    OBTAIN_END --> OBTAIN_MID[OBTAIN MID-POINT GIMBAL ANGLES]
    OBTAIN_MID --> OA10[OA10: (U, SC00) COMPUTE SIN/COS OF Z GIMBAL ANGLE]
    OA10 --> OA12[OA12: (U, SC00) COMPUTE SIN/COS OF Y GIMBAL ANGLE]
    OA12 --> EXIT_OA014[EXIT OA014]
    
    START_OA16[START OA16] --> COMPUTE_ALT[COMPUTE VEHICLE ALTITUDE EQ. 5.4.8]
    COMPUTE_ALT --> CORR_PASS
    CORR_PASS -- YES --> TELEMET[TELEMET ALTIMETER]
    CORR_PASS -- NO --> TELEMET
    
    TELEMET --> ALT_GTR{ALTITUDE GREATER THAN HIGH LIMIT}
    ALT_GTR -- YES --> SET_ATM_ZERO[SET ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY TO ZERO EQ. 5.4.9]
    ALT_GTR -- NO --> ALT_LSS{ALTITUDE LESS THAN LOW LIMIT}
    ALT_LSS -- YES --> SET_ATM_CONST[SET ATM. DENSITY TO CONSTANT EQ. 5.4.9]
    ALT_LSS -- NO --> COMPUTE_ATM[COMPUTE ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY EQ. 5.4.9]
    COMPUTE_ATM --> COMPUTE_REL[COMPUTE RELATIVE VELOCITY EQ. 5.4.10]
    COMPUTE_REL --> COMPUTE_COS[COMPUTE THE COS OF THE ANGLE OF ATTACK EQ. 5.4.11]
    COMPUTE_COS --> COMPUTE_DRAG[COMPUTE THE DRAG COEFF. OF THE VEHICLE EQ. 5.4.12]
    COMPUTE_DRAG --> DO_5412[DO 5.4.12]
    
    DO_5413[DO 5.4.13] --> COMP_X[COMP X DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13]
    COMP_X --> COMP_Y[COMP Y DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13]
    COMP_Y --> COMP_Z[COMP Z DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13]
    COMP_Z --> EXIT_OA25[EXIT OA25]

The flowchart is titled "CRBIT ACCELERATIONS (OA)" and is labeled with a page number "2". It consists of several interconnected steps:

  • START OA01: Initiates the process, leading to a decision point "MID-POINT PASS".
  • MID-POINT PASS: If "YES", it proceeds to "CORRECTOR END-POINT NAVIGATION PASS". If "NO", it goes to "OBTAIN END-POINT GIMBAL ANGLES", then "OBTAIN MID-POINT GIMBAL ANGLES", and finally to "OA10: (U, SC00) COMPUTE SIN/COS OF Z GIMBAL ANGLE".
  • START OA16: Initiates the process, leading to "COMPUTE VEHICLE ALTITUDE EQ. 5.4.8", then to "CORRECTOR END-POINT NAVIGATION PASS".
  • CORRECTOR END-POINT NAVIGATION PASS: If "YES", it leads to "(U, TROD) TELEMET ALTIMETER". If "NO", it leads to "(U, TROD) TELEMET ALTIMETER".
  • (U, TROD) TELEMET ALTIMETER: Leads to a decision point "ALTITUDE GREATER THAN HIGH LIMIT".
  • ALTITUDE GREATER THAN HIGH LIMIT: If "YES", it leads to "SET ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY TO ZERO EQ. 5.4.9". If "NO", it leads to "ALTITUDE LESS THAN LOW LIMIT".
  • ALTITUDE LESS THAN LOW LIMIT: If "YES", it leads to "SET ATM. DENSITY TO CONSTANT EQ. 5.4.9". If "NO", it leads to "COMPUTE ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY EQ. 5.4.9".
  • COMPUTE ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY EQ. 5.4.9: Leads to "COMPUTE RELATIVE VELOCITY EQ. 5.4.10", then "COMPUTE THE COS OF THE ANGLE OF ATTACK EQ. 5.4.11", then "COMPUTE THE DRAG COEFF. OF THE VEHICLE EQ. 5.4.12".
  • COMPUTE THE DRAG COEFF. OF THE VEHICLE EQ. 5.4.12: Leads to "DO 5.4.12".
  • DO 5.4.13: Leads to "COMP X DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13", then "COMP Y DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13", then "COMP Z DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13", and finally "EXIT OA25".
  • EXIT OA014: Terminates the process.
  • EXIT OA25: Terminates the process.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Orbital Guidance routine is to compute the desired vehicle attitude during periods when no propulsion thrust is available and attitude control is provided by the APS system.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
M.OG00Phase 1 via Non-Interrupt Sequencer once per computation cycle*
(when queued-in). Entered once per second during Phase 2 via*
once per second Timer 2 control module.

U.FD00Fixed Point Divide Utility
U.MM00Matrix Multiply Utility
U.SR00Square Root Utility
M.CC00Chi Computations
M.CC10Chi Telemetry
U.TR00Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility
U.FR00Attitude Freeze Utility
U.AT00Arctangent Utility
U.SC00Sine-Cosine Utility

The 'ACCUMULATE' block has a loop: if 'NO', it checks 'OR 1/SEC EMR TO 60 SEC EMR WORD'. If 'YES', it proceeds to 'CR 1/SEC EMR TO DARK PERIOD EMR WORD' and then 'RETURN'. chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The Square Root Utility computes the square root of an input argument.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Upon entry the input argument must be in the accumulator and the first guess of the square root in the utility temporary location, D.VUTB.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The octal value of the first guess must not be less than one-half of the octal value of the input argument; otherwise, an illegal divide will occur which will cause the square root output to be set to the largest possible value.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Upon exit, the square root of the input argument is in the accumulator.

chunks.label: Diagram
chunks.content:
graph TD; START([START U.SR00]) --> V1(( )); V1 --> SAVE[SAVE RETURN LINKAGE]; SAVE --> V2(( )); V2 --> NEGATIVE{NEGATIVE ARGUMENT}; NEGATIVE -- YES --> RETURN1([RETURN]); NEGATIVE -- NO --> V3(( )); V3 --> ILLEGAL{WILL INPUT VALUES RESULT IN ILLEGAL DIVIDE}; ILLEGAL -- YES --> RETURN1; ILLEGAL -- NO --> V4(( )); V4 --> SR05[SR05]; SR05 --> PERFORM[PERFORM SQUARE ROOT ALGORITHM EQ.13.5.1]; PERFORM --> V5(( )); V5 --> NEGATIVE2{ALGORITHM RESULT NEGATIVE}; NEGATIVE2 -- YES --> RETURN1; NEGATIVE2 -- NO --> V6(( )); V6 --> ITERATIONS{HAVE 3 ITERATIONS BEEN PERFORMED}; ITERATIONS -- YES --> RETURN1; ITERATIONS -- NO --> SR05; SR05 --> RETURN2([RETURN]); ILLEGAL --> SR10[SR10]; SR10 --> OVERFLOW[OVERFLOW PROTECTION SET TO LARGE NUMBER]; OVERFLOW --> RETURN3([RETURN]);

The flowchart, titled "SQUARE ROOT UTILITY (SR)", outlines the following steps:

  • START U.SR00: The initial entry point.
  • SAVE RETURN LINKAGE: A process step that saves the return linkage.
  • NEGATIVE ARGUMENT: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it continues to the next step.
  • WILL INPUT VALUES RESULT IN ILLEGAL DIVIDE: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it continues to the next step.
  • SR05: A process step that performs the square root algorithm (Equation 13.5.1).
  • ALGORITHM RESULT NEGATIVE: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it continues to the next step.
  • HAVE 3 ITERATIONS BEEN PERFORMED: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it loops back to the SR05 step.
  • RETURN: The first return point, reached from the NEGATIVE ARGUMENT, WILL INPUT VALUES RESULT IN ILLEGAL DIVIDE, or ALGORITHM RESULT NEGATIVE steps.
  • SR10: A process step that sets overflow protection to a large number.
  • OVERFLOW PROTECTION SET TO LARGE NUMBER: A process step that follows the SR10 step.
  • RETURN: The final return point, reached from the OVERFLOW PROTECTION SET TO LARGE NUMBER step.

1. (1) This module will guarantee all switch selector DOM telemetry.
  2. (2) All switch selector functions and their associated time of issuance are contained in a set of Switch Selector tables referenced by this module for processing.

chunks.label: Section-Header
chunks.content: Switch Selector Nominal and Alternate Event Tables

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
1. 1. The events per mission ICD are to be entered in a nominal event table.
  2. 2. The switch selector program is to have the capability to issue events other than the nominal table.

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
1. 1. The events are to be entered with delta times referenced to the time the alternate event table is initiated.
  2. 2. All alternate event tables are to be terminated when a new time base is initiated.

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
1. a. The nominal event table is considered as class 0.
  2. b. All alternate event tables may be started when the Switch Selector module is operating from the class 0 table.

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
1. a. Class 1 tables will be started immediately upon request.
  2. b. If a switch selector is active, a special entry is made to the forced reset operation and the alternate sequence is started.
  3. c. The interrupted sequence(s) will not be reentered, and upon completion, the Class 1 alternate sequence will assume a class 0 priority level.
  4. d. The nominal S-IVB cutoff switch selector has the highest priority of all switch selector commands.

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
1. a. A class 2 sequence interrupts the current switch selector sequence and must be issued in its entirety.
  2. b. If a switch selector is active, a special entry is made to the forced reset operation and the alternate sequence is started.
  3. c. Upon completion of the class 2 event table control is returned to the table that was in effect when the class 2 table was initiated.

chunks.label: List-Group
chunks.content:
• d. All events that are late because the class 2 sequence was initiated will be issued at the maximum switch selector rate until normal timing can be resumed.
  • 3. Class 3
    • a. Class 3 events are to be issued at maximum switch selector rate.
    • b. Class 3 tables may be started when the switch selector program is operating from a class 0, or class 4 table.
    • c. Upon completion of the class 3 event table, control is returned to the table that was in effect when the class 3 table was initiated.
    • d. All events that are late because the class 3 sequence was initiated will be issued at the maximum switch selector rate.
  • 4. Class 4
    • a. Class 4 tables are to be concurrent event tables with no restriction on number of events.
    • b. Class 4 tables may be started when the switch selector program is operating from any class table.
    • c. The events of a class 4 table are to be merged with the events of the table that the switch selector is operating from.
    • d. The concurrent table (Class 4) has the lowest priority when the times of the read operation are equivalent.

  • Class 3 Alternate event table of one or two events

The flowchart describes the logic of a Switch Selector Processor (SS). It begins at a START block (SS00). A decision point (NORMAL SWITCH SELECTOR) leads to either a check for requested alternate sequences (SS20) or processing the normal switch selector (SS10). Both paths lead to a decision point (BYPASS THE HUNG STAGE TEST). If YES, it proceeds to execute the hung stage test (SS40); if NO, it also proceeds to SS40. From SS40, the process moves to issue the stage and address (SS50), then verify the address (SS55). A decision point (ADDRESS FEEDBACK GOOD) follows. If NO, it proceeds to issue the read command (SS70); if YES, it also proceeds to SS70. Finally, it issues the reset (SS75) and exits (EXIT RETURN).

The flowchart, titled "SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS)", details the logic for processing switch selector entries. It begins with two parallel paths for "CLASS 4 TABLE ADVANCE ENTRY 1" and "CLASS 4 TABLE ADVANCE ENTRY 2". The first path involves updating time and stage, advancing the switch selector table, and saving time and stage information. The second path involves updating time and stage, saving return hop constants, and resetting the class 4 in progress flag. A central decision point determines if an entry is a "SPECIAL ENTRY" or a "TIME WORD". If a "TIME WORD", it checks if sectors can be changed. If so, it resets the CLA pointer to the beginning of the sector and updates time and stage. If not, it checks if it's the end of a table entry. If yes, it resets the class 4 in progress flag. If no, it processes a non-special entry and updates the SS table pointer. The process concludes with exits to SS2090 or SS2070.

The flowchart describes the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS) logic. It begins with a START block (M, SS30) leading to setting the SWITCH SELECTOR HUNG STAGE. This triggers SS3000 (SET SWITCH SELECTOR ACTIVE FLAG), which leads to SS3010 (OBTAIN STAGE AND ADDRESS WORD), then REFORMAT STAGE AND ADDRESS WORD, and finally SAVE STAGE & ADDR. IN TRUE FORM, which feeds into SS3020 (RO). From SS3020, the process branches based on whether the stage is zero. If YES, it proceeds to RESET SWITCH SELECTOR ACTIVE FLAG, then ADVANCE SWITCH SELECTOR TABLE (ENTRY 1), and finally EXIT SS0000. If NO, it proceeds to SS3030 (ARE STAGES POWERED). If YES, it sets bias for address scheduling and exits SS0000. If NO, it alters EXM to not execute PIO 036 (LOAD SS), then SS3040 (ALTER EXM TO EXECUTE PIO 036), then SS3060 (BYPASS HUNG STAGE TEST). If YES, it exits SS4000. If NO, it checks if we are in a repeatable SIM flight. If YES, it exits SS4000. If NO, it reads the SWITCH SELECTOR FEEDBACK REGISTER, then checks if there is a HUNG STAGE. If YES, it proceeds to SS3070 (ISSUE RESET), then SS3090 (ISSUE STAGE AND ADDRESS (M, SS40)), and finally a DO block. If NO, it proceeds to SS3087 and exits SS4000.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility module is to guarantee that telemetry items are not output faster than the maximum rate allowed. When the time for telemetry occurs, the module sets the LVDA Mode Register to the required bit configuration and returns to the calling program module which immediately issues the telemetry.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content:
U.TR10 Dummy entry to bypass minor loop error telemetry *
if guidance failure occurs. *

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: Time of last telemetry output (D.VTD) must be initialized to zero at start of mission.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: This module should be accessed only through the telemetry macro, TELM, to assure the entry and return requirements of the module are met.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: If the TELM macro is not used, the data sector containing the required mode register bit configuration for the item to be telemetered must be in effect on entry to this module. Upon return the next two instructions executed in the calling program module must be CLA and PIO to complete the telemetry operation while interrupt protection is still in effect.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: All interrupts are inhibited (MPY instruction) during the test for telemetry output time. When time for telemetry occurs, interrupt protection is extended (DIV instruction) over the total telemetry output operation. This includes the first two instructions executed in the calling module upon return. Interrupts are periodically allowed during the delay loop.

chunks.content:
graph TD; Start([START U.TROO]) --> Inhibit([INHIBIT INTERRUPTS]); Inhibit --> ReadClock([READ REAL TIME CLOCK]); ReadClock --> Decision{SUFFICIENT DELAY FOR TELEMETRY}; Decision -- YES --> SetMode([SET MODE REGISTER]); Decision -- NO --> Delay([DELAY FOR TELEMETRY]); Delay --> B1Out([B1]); SetMode --> UpdateTime([UPDATE TELEMETRY TIME]); UpdateTime --> Exit([EXIT RETURN]);

The flowchart illustrates the logic of the REAL-TIME TELEMETRY DELAY UTILITY (TR). It begins with a 'START U.TROO' block, which leads to 'INHIBIT INTERRUPTS'. This step is influenced by TR10 and B1. Following this, the system 'READ REAL TIME CLOCK'. A decision point then asks if there is 'SUFFICIENT DELAY FOR TELEMETRY'. If 'YES', it proceeds to 'SET MODE REGISTER', then 'UPDATE TELEMETRY TIME', and finally 'EXIT RETURN'. If 'NO', it enters a 'DELAY FOR TELEMETRY' block, which is also influenced by TR20 and TR10, and has a B1 output. The flowchart uses dotted boxes for process blocks and a diamond for the decision point, with arrows indicating the sequence of operations.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: The function of the Time Tilt Guidance Module is to generate steering commands (guidance chi's) as a function of time from liftoff through the S-IB burn.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D.KT1 Time Base 1 start time from GRR

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D.VXS X component of radius vector, in S-system

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D.GTRY Distance from geocentric radius to top of gantry

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D.VGCY Guidance Chi Y (Desired pitch gimbal angle)

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle)

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D.VTAR, V.TTST, and V.TTF must be initialized to pre-stored values at mission start.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: D.VEOT and F.TTA must be initialized to zero at mission start.

chunks.label: Text
chunks.content: On indication from the Discrete Processor module that engine out has occurred, the Time Tilt Guidance module will freeze guidance chi's for a specified time, and then continue normal time tilt guidance. Variable scaling is incorporated through the use of pseudo-variables. Initialization of the various pitch time tilt segments and yaw time tilt segments for the Time Tilt Guidance module will be executed as a function of time via a time test in the Time Tilt Guidance module.

The flowchart, titled "TIME TILT GUIDANCE (TT)", begins at "START TT51". It proceeds through a series of decision points: "ENGINE OUT OCCURRED IN FIRST SEGMENT" and "ENGINE OUT OCCURRED IN 2ND SEGMENT". If either is "YES", the flow continues to "ENGINE OUT OCCURRED IN 3RD SEGMENT". If "NO" for any of these, the process moves to "STZ DELTA FREEZE TIME TO ZERO EQ.4.4.4", which then leads to "EXIT TT160". If "YES" for the 3rd segment, it proceeds to "TT140 CALC DEL FREEZE TIME FOR 1ST SEG EQ.4.4.4", then "TT150 CALC DEL FREEZE TIME FOR 2ND SEG EQ.4.4.4", and finally "TT160 COMPUTE TOTAL FREEZE TIME EQ.4.4.5". From "TT160 COMPUTE TOTAL FREEZE TIME", the flow moves to "TT165 CALCULATE TILT ARREST TIME EQ.4.4.6", then "ZERO ENGINE OUT TIME", and finally "EXIT TT60".

The left path starts with 'START M.TU00', followed by 'INHIBIT INTERRUPTS', 'READ REAL TIME CLOCK FOR TIME REFERENCE', 'ENABLE INTERRUPTS', 'TELEMETER REAL TIME CLOCK', 'COMPUTE NAV EXTRAP. TOTAL TIME IN MISSION', 'COMPUTE TIME IN TIME BASE', 'TELEMETER TIME IN TIME BASE', 'CALCULATE TIME IN TIME BASE BIASED', and finally 'TELEMETER TIME IN TIME BASE BIASED'. TOTAL TIME IN MIS', followed by 'TELEMETER TIME BASE START TIME', 'FORM DATA COMPRESSION TIME WORD', 'SYSTEM TIME UPDATE', and ends with 'EXIT RETURN'. Both paths converge at the final output step.
